meta.title: Competitor Radar
meta.niche: Cloud monitoring, observability, and application performance management (APM) software

analysis.summary: Most rivals are chasing AI agent observability. New Relic is also going straight at Datadog buyers, while Datadog has no comparison pages of its own.

points.text: New Relic published three "Datadog vs." pages for people weighing Datadog against rivals. Datadog has no comparison pages in this set.
Dynatrace added 61 new pages, with bulk launches of 31 and 30 pages and Google Cloud pages in four languages.
Datadog's 21 new pages lean on AI agent how-tos, but New Relic, Grafana Labs and Dynatrace also push AI observability.

Datadog.play: Mixes AI agent how-tos with RUM and synthetic content, plus new government landing pages.

New Relic.play: Targets rivals with comparison pages and sells AI-ready 'trusted context' through opinion pieces and product news.

Dynatrace.play: Bulk-launches translated cloud and partner pages, backed by CVE alerts and a 466% ROI study.

Splunk.play: Published nothing new and updated nothing. Seven old pages were removed, including State of observability.

Grafana Labs.play: Ships product news, AI and agent landing pages, and five rival comparisons. 110 pages were removed.
Grafana Labs.aimed: Cost-minded engineers and open source users

Elastic Observability.play: Mostly release notes and customer stories, plus analyst-ranking and public sector news.

Sumo Logic.play: Refreshes DojoAI agent pages (16 updated, 6 new), mostly security-focused, and adds AI credit pricing.

shared.title: AI agent observability
shared.text: Datadog, New Relic, Grafana Labs, Dynatrace and Sumo Logic all publish pages on monitoring AI agents. Expect a crowded topic, so Datadog needs sharper, hands-on proof.

shared.title: Rival comparison pages
shared.text: New Relic has seven comparison pages and Grafana has five. Sumo Logic has one, Splunk vs Sumo Logic. Datadog has none, so rivals write the story about Datadog.

shared.title: Cloud and partner tie-ins
shared.text: Each company announces a cloud or partner link: Oracle, OCI, Google Cloud, AWS, or Google Distributed Cloud. Buyers on those clouds get pages written for them.

gaps.title: Multilingual content
gaps.text: Only Dynatrace publishes Spanish, Japanese and Chinese pages and webinars. No Datadog pages in this set are translated, so non-English buyers are open.

gaps.title: Datadog's own head-to-head pages
gaps.text: New Relic is the only one writing "Datadog vs." pages. Datadog could publish its own fair, detailed comparisons and own that search.

gaps.title: Fast CVE response guides
gaps.text: Dynatrace has three CVE pages and Sumo Logic has one. Datadog has none in this set, though it publishes supply chain and prompt injection content.

versus.New Relic: Publishes more (31 new vs 21), leaning on opinion and comparisons. Datadog leans on how-tos and has no comparison pages.
versus.Dynatrace: Much bigger output (61 new, 10 updated) with translated pages and bulk launches. Datadog ships fewer pages and updated none.
versus.Splunk: No new or updated pages this period, so Datadog is the only one of the two publishing.
versus.Grafana Labs: Publishes 69 new pages to Datadog's 21, with five comparison pages and heavy product news. Datadog is lighter on both.
versus.Elastic Observability: Small site (46 pages), mostly release notes and customer stories. Datadog publishes far more how-to and product content.
versus.Sumo Logic: Mostly refreshes old pages (16 updated, 6 new) around DojoAI and security. Datadog does the reverse: all new, no updates.
